title: Rhinoplasty, aka Nose Jobs
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss rhinoplasty (nose jobs), opening with banter about the word "schnoz" and a teaser for a grilled cheese listener mail segment. They cover the reasons people get nose jobs (injury, birth ethnicity, syphilis-related collapse, cosmetic and medical reasons), changing cultural attitudes from the mid-century boom to today, US and international statistics, and the history from the Indian surgeon Sushruta and the Indian flap, through the Italian flap, to 19th-century surgeons John Orlando Roe and Jacques Joseph and the rise of unlicensed "beauty doctors." They explain nose anatomy (nasal bone, cartilage, rhinion, columella, septum, lateral cartilages), open versus closed rhinoplasty, recovery, cosmetic versus medical (deviated septum) reasons, costs, ethnic rhinoplasty and the history of racial passing, celebrity regret (Jennifer Grey, Bella Hadid), Iranian rates, and social media targeting of teens for cosmetic surgery ads. The episode closes with a listener mail round-up of grilled cheese tips.

segments.title: Opening banter and nose job terminology
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about the word schnoz and Martin Short's Saturday Night Live sketch, then introduce rhinoplasty, its Greek roots, and the shift from 'rhinoplasty' to 'nose sculpting.'

segments.title: Reasons for nose jobs and changing attitudes
segments.summary: They list reasons people get nose jobs: historical punishment, war injuries, ethnic features, syphilis-related collapse, and cosmetic goals like facial balance, width, humps, and droopy tips. They discuss how mid-century American attitudes gave way to a desire for a tamed, more natural nose and a focus on self-image.

segments.title: Nose job statistics
segments.summary: They cite US figures for cosmetic procedures and nose jobs by sex, age, region, and ethnicity, then discuss the unreliability of international rankings led by Brazil, with the US, Mexico, Iran, and Turkey also high.

segments.title: Ancient origins: Sushruta and the Indian flap
segments.summary: The hosts describe Sushruta, called the father of cosmetic surgery, who rebuilt noses using a cheek skin flap documented in ancient texts. They read a description of the Indian flap technique, including the use of tubes and stitching.

segments.title: Italian flap and 19th-century cosmetic surgery
segments.summary: The Italian surgeon Gaspare Tagliacozzi used the upper arm for the flap. In the late nineteenth century, surgeons including John Orlando Roe and Jacques Joseph developed aesthetic surgery, Joseph also worked on World War One facial reconstruction, and the resulting demand gave rise to unlicensed beauty doctors using paraffin and other unsafe injections.

segments.title: Nose anatomy and types of rhinoplasty
segments.summary: They walk through the parts of the nose: nasal bone, cartilage, rhinion, columella, septum, and tip. They explain that plastic refers to molding rather than plastic material, describe how septum problems and cocaine can cause perforation, and compare open and closed rhinoplasty.

segments.title: Recovery, medical rhinoplasty, and Josh's septum story
segments.summary: They discuss recovery time, avoiding blowing the nose, and stents, and then distinguish cosmetic from medical rhinoplasty for deviated septum, which insurance may cover. Josh describes his own deviated septum diagnosis and a friend's difficult recovery.

segments.title: Costs and personal reflections on noses
segments.summary: They give typical costs of roughly five to ten thousand dollars with higher prices in some cities, and discuss traveling for surgery. Josh reflects on his own nose and a childhood Valentine's Day memory.

segments.title: Ethnic rhinoplasty, racial passing, and generational change
segments.summary: They discuss ethnic rhinoplasty and the 19th-century idea that nose shape signaled moral character, Jacques Joseph's language about Jewish noses, and the mid-century practice of giving nose jobs to Jewish teens. They contrast this with younger generations who reject the pressure.

segments.title: Celebrity regrets, Iran, and teens targeted by ads
segments.summary: They discuss Jennifer Grey's nose job and career effects, Bella Hadid's regret, reverse nose jobs, and rhinoplasty rates in Iran linked to hijab rules. They close with concerns about TikTok serving plastic surgery ads to users as young as fourteen.

segments.title: Grilled cheese listener mail
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read listener tips for grilled cheese sandwiches, including manchego, maple syrup with Colby, Dijon mustard, garlic cream cheese, mayo instead of butter, and salsa for dipping, plus a Sims grilled cheese aspiration anecdote.
